Nixie HV supply: every decision, switchable

A 170 V supply small enough to hide behind a side-view tube and under an IN-12, built around the Omnixie NCH8200HV's control loop. Each choice is listed with its reason and what it costs. Flip options and the cost, board size, fit and current draw update; the same switches generate the KiCad schematic and a placed board, as one board or as two stacked with the parts inside.

KiCad schematic and board for this combination

Both files are built for the switches above. Save them as nixie_hv.kicad_sch and nixie_hv.kicad_pcb in a project folder from nixie_hv_kicad.zip, which holds the libraries, the design rules and these generators as scripts. The board is the by-function arrangement at the width limit set beside the preview: every footprint placed on its side with its nets assigned and the outline drawn, ready to route. It has no tracks, vias or copper pours. A stacked build is one file with two outlines, each drawn from its parts side.

        How the numbers are worked out. Standby adds datasheet shutdown and leakage currents. Idle adds the feedback divider (170 V across 20.1 MΩ, taken through the converter at 80 %) and the MAX668's 0.22 mA at its supply rail. Output current assumes discontinuous conduction at 100 kHz and 90 % duty, limited by the transformer's 2.7 A, with 80 % efficiency throughout. Board size is the smallest outline into which every footprint courtyard fits on two sides; thickness assumes a 0.8 mm board. A stack is two such boards, the gap between them (the tallest inside part plus 0.2 mm, or with a slot the transformer's height less one board) and anything mounted on the outside faces; the ends of the pin posts and their solder are not counted.
